     9	/-!
    10	# Finite subsets in affine opens
    11	
    12	`Scheme.FiniteInAffine X` is the action-free geometric condition behind the
    13	finite-Galois quotient construction: every finite subset of `X` lies in one
    14	affine open.  For a finite Galois extension, this immediately supplies
    15	`SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` for every action on `X`.
    16	
    17	The property is stated independently of Picard data.  In particular, it is a
    18	conclusion to be proved for a representing scheme, not an additional field of
    19	the representability datum.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	open CategoryTheory
    27	open AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
    30	
    31	/-- Every finite subset of a scheme is contained in a single affine open. -/
    32	def FiniteInAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop :=
    33	  ∀ s : Set X, s.Finite → ∃ U : X.affineOpens, s ⊆ U.1
    34	
    35	/-- An affine scheme satisfies `FiniteInAffine`. -/
    36	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] :
    37	    FiniteInAffine X :=
    38	  fun _ _ ↦ ⟨⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top X⟩, fun _ _ ↦ trivial⟩
    39	
    40	/-- `FiniteInAffine` is invariant under isomorphism. -/
    41	theorem finiteInAffine_of_iso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (e : X ≅ Y)
    42	    (h : FiniteInAffine X) : FiniteInAffine Y := by
    43	  intro s hs
    44	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (e.hom.base ⁻¹' s)
    45	    (hs.preimage (TopCat.homeoOfIso ((Scheme.forgetToTop).mapIso e)).injective.injOn)
    46	  refine ⟨⟨e.hom ''ᵁ U.1, U.2.image_of_isOpenImmersion e.hom⟩, ?_⟩
    47	  intro y hy
    48	  exact ⟨e.inv.base y, hU (by simpa using hy), by simp⟩
    49	
    50	/-- `FiniteInAffine` descends along an affine morphism. -/
    51	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    52	    [IsAffineHom f] (h : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by
    53	  intro s hs
    54	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (f.base '' s) (hs.image _)
    55	  exact ⟨⟨f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1, U.2.preimage f⟩, fun x hx ↦ hU ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩⟩
    56	
    57	/-- An object affine over a field spectrum satisfies `FiniteInAffine`. -/
    58	theorem finiteInAffine_left_of_isAffineHom {k : Type u} [Field k]
    59	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsAffineHom X.hom] :
    60	    FiniteInAffine X.left :=
    61	  haveI := isAffine_of_isAffineHom X.hom
    62	  finiteInAffine_of_isAffine _
    63	
    64	/-- `FiniteInAffine` supplies the orbit condition for every finite-Galois
    65	semilinear action on the scheme. -/
    66	theorem orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine
    67	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    68	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
    69	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    70	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (h : FiniteInAffine X) :
    71	    rho.OrbitsInAffineOpen where
    72	  exists_affineOpen x := by
    73	    obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ :=
    74	      h (Set.range fun gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L ↦ (rho.act gamma).hom.base x)
    75	        (Set.finite_range _)
    76	    exact ⟨U, fun gamma ↦ hU ⟨gamma, rfl⟩⟩
    77	
    78	end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

   161	group over an algebraically closed field lies in one affine open. -/
   162	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAlgClosed_of_irreducible
   163	    (G : Over (Spec (.of K))) [GrpObj G] [IsAlgClosed K]

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AtlasCompactFromClass
     7	-- Imported so that the coverage lemma this file's docstrings CITE is in its own import closure:
     8	-- a cited name that resolves only by `grep` is a name this file cannot see, and that failure mode
     9	-- has recurred in this project (I-1073, I-0994).  `pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` is the
    10	-- converse that makes single-index coverage equivalent to unrestricted one-chart coverage, which
    11	-- is why `Finite ι` below is not cheap.
    12	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling
    13	
    14	/-!
    15	# The per-chart half of `hcpt` was NOT free: the charts are OPENS, and openness needs noetherianity
    16	
    17	Three files price the atlas's `CompactSpace` input, and all three split it the same way: the
    18	per-chart half is "free at the divisor-representability lane's own carrier", the index-finiteness
    19	half is the obstruction.  The first half of that split is **about the wrong object**.
    20	
    21	`Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean`'s `Discharged` section exhibits
    22	`CompactSpace (divSchemeOver k A B n r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂).left` by `inferInstance` and calls it "the
    23	compactness input of `JacobianData.ofCharts`'s finite route, at the same carrier".  But the charts
    24	of the atlas are not the representing objects.  `mixedParamChart` is
    25	`restrictChart (abelSigmaChart …) (V i)`, whose source is `yoneda.obj ((V i : Scheme))` — an
    26	**open subscheme** of `(D i).left`.  So `compactSpace_of_finite_atlas`'s hypothesis
    27	`∀ i, CompactSpace (X i)` is compactness of `(V i : Scheme)`, and *that* is not an instance:
    28	
    29	> `example … (V : (divSchemeOver …).left.Opens) : CompactSpace (V : Scheme) := by infer_instance`
    30	
    31	fails.  Compactness does not pass to open subspaces, so the sentence three sites carry is true of
    32	`divSchemeOver` and false of the object the hypothesis is about.
    33	
    34	**How large the gap is depends on a claim this tree does not prove, and an earlier version of this
    35	header asserted it as fact.**  That version said `V ≠ ⊤` is *forced*, because "the `hf` certificate
    36	is false for the Abel chart at `V = ⊤`", citing `Pic0ChartPair.lean:134`.  That line is a
    37	docstring assertion, not a theorem: there is **no** `¬ IsOpenImmersion.presheaf` declaration
    38	anywhere in this project (measured by search, not by grep for one spelling).  So the honest form is
    39	weaker — for `V = ⊤` the ambient instance would suffice and the gap would be invisible, and nothing
    40	in Lean rules that `V` out.  What *is* certain is that the lemma below is needed for a general `V`,
    41	which is what `mixedParamChart` quantifies over; whether `V = ⊤` is admissible is open.
    42	
    43	## What closes it, and it is not a new hypothesis
    44	
    45	`DivScheme` is a *noetherian* scheme, and on a noetherian space every subset is compact.
    46	
    47	* `IsLocallyNoetherian` comes from `LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian` applied to
    48	  `locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom` over the noetherian base `Spec k` — a field is a
    49	  noetherian ring, so nothing is assumed of the curve.
    50	* with `compactSpace_divScheme` that is `IsNoetherian`, hence `NoetherianSpace`, hence
    51	  `NoetherianSpace.isCompact` applies to the carrier of any `V`.
    52	
    53	So the per-chart half is genuinely free — but by noetherianity of the divisor scheme, not by the
    54	instance the three sites cite.  `compactSpace_isOpen_divSchemeOver` below is that step, and
    55	`compactSpace_glued_of_finite_mixedParamChart` feeds it to `compactSpace_of_finite_atlas`.
    56	
    57	## What this does NOT do
    58	
    59	**`Finite ι` is not discharged and I do not claim it is.**  Dropping it makes
    60	`compactSpace_glued_of_finite_mixedParamChart` fail to elaborate (measured), which is the point:
    61	after this file the atlas's compactness input costs *index finiteness alone*.  That is a strict
    62	subtraction from the three-route picture — the class route's `hcl`
    63	(`Pic0AtlasCompactFromClass.lean`) and the Abel image are no longer the only ways to pay it at a
    64	finite atlas — and it is **not** a producer of `hcpt` for the classical class-indexed atlas, which
    65	has no finiteness.
    66	
    67	**AND FINITENESS IS NOT CHEAP FOR THE ASSEMBLY — but that caveat is about the assembly, NOT about
    68	the compactness lemma, and an earlier version of this header attached it to both.**  A
    69	`PUnit`-indexed atlas is `Finite` and elaborates against `jacobianDataOfFiniteMixedParamCharts`
    70	(probed), so it looks as though finiteness could be met by simply taking one chart.  For the
    71	*assembly* it cannot be met that way: per inbox `I-1389`, single-index coverage implies
    72	**unrestricted one-chart coverage** through the landed converse
    73	`pointwise_of_pointwise_restrictChart` (`Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling.lean`), and one-chart coverage is
    74	the configuration the heterogeneous atlas exists to avoid needing
    75	(`Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean`, `Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean`,
    76	`Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean`).  Neither those files nor `I-1389` *proves* the non-uniformity they
    77	assert, so whether a finite atlas covers is open in both directions.
    78	
    79	**The compactness lemma is coverage-free, which is stronger than the caveat suggested** (`I-1430`).
    80	`compactSpace_glued_of_finite_mixedParamChart` carries the `IsLocallySurjective` instance binder
    81	only to match the assembly's shape: the binder is **idle**, and the statement compiles with it
    82	deleted (measured).  `glueData` does not depend on coverage — mathlib introduces that instance
    83	only at `representableBy` (`Sites/Representability.lean`).  So `hcpt` costs `Finite ι` *and
    84	nothing about coverage*; the I-1389 coupling bites when the assembly consumes coverage for `rep`,
    85	not here.  The binder is kept so that a consumer holding the assembly's hypotheses can apply this
    86	lemma without reshaping them, and this paragraph exists so nobody prices the idle binder as a cost.
    87	
    88	No claim is made here that a finite atlas exists.
    89	
    90	No antecedent of the seam moves.  `rep`, `IsChartUniv` and Zariski-local surjectivity are
    91	untouched, and this file produces no `JacobianData` at any curve.
    92	
    93	## Main declarations
    94	
    95	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyNoetherian_divSchemeOver` — the divisor scheme is locally
    96	  noetherian, from `LocallyOfFiniteType` over the noetherian base.
    97	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isNoetherian_divSchemeOver` — and noetherian, with `compactSpace_divScheme`.
    98	* `AlgebraicGeometry.compactSpace_isOpen_divSchemeOver` — **the step the three sites skipped**:
    99	  every open of the divisor scheme is a compact space.
   100	* `AlgebraicGeometry.compactSpace_of_representableBy` — and it is a property of the **functor**:
   101	  compactness of a representing object transports between representations, the companion of
   102	  `locallyOfFiniteType_of_representableBy`.
   103	* `AlgebraicGeometry.compactSpace_glued_of_finite_mixedParamChart` — `hcpt` for a finite
   104	  mixed-parameter atlas at the divisor-representability carrier, with **no** `hcl` and no Abel
   105	  morphism.
   106	* `AlgebraicGeometry.jacobianDataOfFiniteMixedParamCharts` — the assembly with `hcpt` gone and
   107	  `Finite ι` in its place.
   108	* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_jacobianDataOfFiniteMixedParamCharts` — the consequence for the
   109	  `dat-j.qcfield` row: that row's field is *discharged* at a finite atlas, so `hcl` is what pays it
   110	  at an **infinite** one.
   111	-/

   148	theorem isLocallyNoetherian_divSchemeOver {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]

   152	    (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤)) :

   154	  @LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian _ _ (divSchemeOver k A B n r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂).hom
   155	    (locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom k A B n r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) inferInstance

   161	instance, so `constructor` finds the second field on its own.  Kept as a named theorem because

   167	    (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(divisorSections k B ⊤))
   168	    (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤)) :
   169	    IsNoetherian (divSchemeOver k A B n r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂).left := by
   170	  haveI := isLocallyNoetherian_divSchemeOver k A B n r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂
   171	  constructor

   173	/-- **THE STEP THREE SITES SKIPPED**: every open subscheme of the divisor scheme is a compact
   174	space.
   175	
   176	This is what the atlas's per-chart hypothesis actually asks for, and it is *not* the instance
   177	`CompactSpace (divSchemeOver …).left` that `Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean`'s `Discharged` section
   178	exhibits: compactness does not pass to open subspaces.
   179	
   180	**It needs only LOCAL noetherianity**, not `IsNoetherian`: on a locally noetherian scheme the
   181	inclusion of an open is quasi-compact (mathlib's `quasiCompact_of_noetherianSpace_source` via
   182	`IsLocallyNoetherian`'s affine-local noetherian spaces, stacks 01OX), and
   183	`QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace V.ι` then transports compactness *down* from the
   184	ambient.  An earlier proof here went through `IsNoetherian` → `NoetherianSpace` →
   185	`NoetherianSpace.isCompact`, two hops longer, and made the lemma look as though it needed
   186	compactness of the ambient scheme as a hypothesis rather than as an instance already in scope
   187	(`I-1431`).

   190	the atlas are arbitrary — `mixedParamChart` takes `V : ∀ i, (D i).left.Opens` unconstrained. -/
   191	theorem compactSpace_isOpen_divSchemeOver {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))]
   192	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))] [IsIntegral X]
   193	    (A B : X.CurveDivisor) (n r₁ r₂ : ℕ)
   194	    (b₁ : Module.Basis (Fin r₁) k ↥(divisorSections k B ⊤))
   195	    (b₂ : Module.Basis (Fin r₂) k ↥(divisorSections k (A + B) ⊤))
   196	    (V : (divSchemeOver k A B n r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂).left.Opens) :
   197	    CompactSpace (V : Scheme.{u}) := by
   198	  haveI := isLocallyNoetherian_divSchemeOver k A B n r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂
   199	  exact QuasiCompact.compactSpace_of_compactSpace V.ι

   203	/-! ## The per-chart half belongs to the FUNCTOR, not to `divSchemeOver`
   204	
   205	The section above is stated at `divSchemeOver`, which is where the divisor-representability lane's
   206	producers land — but that carrier is not where the property lives, and `Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean`
   207	had already made exactly this argument for the *other* finiteness input:
   208	`locallyOfFiniteType_of_representableBy` proves `hD` transports between any two representations of
   209	`divFunctor C π n`, with a header paragraph on why a carrier-specific argument is the worse one.
   210	
   211	Compactness transports the same way and for the same reason, so the same paragraph applies.
   212	Recorded after an audit observed that this file's correction had inherited the narrowness of the
   213	claim it was correcting (`I-1431`, `I-1433`): the wrong-object defect was fixed at one carrier,
   214	while the fix's own scope went unexamined. -/
   215	
   216	section Transport
   217	
   218	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
   219	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]
   220	
   221	variable (C π) in
   222	/-- **Compactness of a representing object is a property of the divisor functor.**
   223	
   224	If `divFunctor C π n` is represented by `D` and by `D'`, and `D'.left` is compact, so is `D.left`.
   225	Representing objects are isomorphic over the base (`Functor.RepresentableBy.uniqueUpToIso`), the
   226	component `e.hom.left` is then an isomorphism of schemes, and compactness transports along the

    11

    13	§2.4): the abstract topological shape that `JacobianData.quasiCompact` consumes to get
    14	quasi-compactness of the Jacobian structure morphism from the Abel image of `Div^g`-lite.

    16	The mathematics is entirely mathlib's: the continuous surjective image of a compact space
    17	is compact (`Function.Surjective.compactSpace`). This file packages that for scheme
    18	morphisms and adds the quasi-compactness corollary over an affine base, so DAT-J's qc
    19	field is a one-line instantiation. It is deliberately **Challenge-free** (mathlib-only, no
    20	curve/Challenge imports) — the DAT-J producer cone must not cycle through `Challenge.lean`
    21	(worksheet §0.5 / risk 1).

    23	## Main results
    24	
    25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.compactSpace_of_surjective`: if `f : X ⟶ Y` is a surjection of
    26	  schemes out of a compact-space source `X`, then `Y` is a compact space.
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_surjective`: a structure morphism `g : Y ⟶ Z` to an
    28	  affine base is quasi-compact as soon as `Y` receives such a surjection. This is the
    29	  shape DAT-J's DJ-1 consumes with `X := Div^g` (`compactSpace_divScheme`), `f := abel`
    30	  the Abel morphism, `g := J.hom`, `Z := Spec k`.

    43	/-- **DJ-0, compact-image half.** If `f : X ⟶ Y` is a surjection of schemes out of a
    44	compact-space source, then the target is a compact space: the underlying map of `f` is a
    45	continuous surjection (`Scheme.Hom.continuous`), and the continuous surjective image of a
    46	compact space is compact (`Function.Surjective.compactSpace`). -/
    47	theorem compactSpace_of_surjective (f : X ⟶ Y) [CompactSpace X]
    48	    (hf : Function.Surjective f.base) : CompactSpace Y :=
    49	  hf.compactSpace f.continuous
    50	
    51	/-- **DJ-0, quasi-compactness corollary.** A structure morphism `g : Y ⟶ Z` to an affine
    52	base is quasi-compact as soon as `Y` receives a surjection `f : X ⟶ Y` from a
    53	compact-space source `X`. Over an affine base, `QuasiCompact g` is exactly `CompactSpace Y`
    54	(`HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine`, the `DivSchemeQProj` pattern), which the
    55	compact-image half supplies.

    57	This is the abstract shape `JacobianData.quasiCompact` consumes: instantiate
    58	`X := Div^g` (compact via `compactSpace_divScheme`), `f := abel` the Abel morphism
    59	(surjective on points, DJ-1), `g := J.hom`, `Z := Spec k`. -/
    60	theorem quasiCompact_of_surjective (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [IsAffine Z]
    61	    [CompactSpace X] (hf : Function.Surjective f.base) : QuasiCompact g :=
    62	  haveI : CompactSpace Y := compactSpace_of_surjective f hf
    63	  HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›
    64

**Exact carrier**

- [`pic0_sepClosed_representableBy`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0SepClosedRepresentable.lean:426) assumes `[Field k] [IsSepClosed k]`, plus proper, smooth relative dimension one, and geometrically irreducible `C`.
- Its result is `Σ J, (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J`. Thus for
  `Jsc := (pic0_sepClosed_representableBy (C := C)).1`, the representation is exactly `.2`.
- Unfolding [`pic0_sepClosed_representableBy_of_isOpen`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0SepClosedRepresentable.lean:412) and [`pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161), `Jsc.left` is definitionally the 01JJ glued scheme for `picRankOneTranslatedChart`; its index is [`PicRankOneTranslatorIndex`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0SepClosedRepresentable.lean:159), the subtype of base Čech-Picard classes of degree `genus C`.
- The LFT field is already proved by [`locallyOfFiniteType_pic0_sepClosed_representableBy`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0SepClosedRepresentable.lean:433).
- No declaration currently proves `QuasiCompact Jsc.hom`.

**Applicable QC criteria**

- [`JacobianData.ofRepresentableBy`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean:71): `rep` and `hlft` instantiate exactly; only `QuasiCompact Jsc.hom` is missing.
- [`quasiCompact_of_pic0_class_surjective`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/JacobianDataQcFromRep.lean:230): applies to `Jsc` once given one fixed divisor scheme, one `lam`, and the residue-field-pinned class lift `hcl`.
- [`quasiCompact_of_extensionTolerant_lift`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/JacobianDataQcFromRep.lean:293): also applies to `Jsc`; its remaining input is
  `∀ y, ∃ T, Nonempty T.left, e : T ⟶ overSpec k κ(y), q : T ⟶ DivScheme, pic0Map C q lam = rep.homEquiv (e ≫ testPoint y)`.
- [`extensionTolerant_of_kappaPinned`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/JacobianDataQcFromRep.lean:307) only converts the stronger pinned hypothesis into that form.
- [`quasiCompact_of_divRep_of_lift`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/JacobianDataQcFromRep.lean:374) produces `lam` from the old `divFunctor C π n` carrier, but the present construction uses widened `divFunctorAff`. It is not the route to revive under protection I-0492 and still leaves `hcl`.
- [`quasiCompact_of_finite_family_pic0_class`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/JacobianDataQcFiniteFamily.lean:155) requires a finite family and pinned lifts. It does not supply an extension-tolerant finite-family variant.
- [`quasiCompact_of_surjective`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/CompactImageQc.lean:60) is the cleanest criterion: a compact source and a point-surjective scheme morphism to `Jsc`.
- The specialized forms [`quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/JacobianDataAbelImage.lean:93) and [`quasiCompact_of_forall_residueField_lift_from_divScheme`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:118) apply but demand the same point-surjectivity or the stronger pinned lifts.
- [`quasiCompact_gluedHom`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean:164) is definitionally about the exact glued carrier, but needs `[Finite PicRankOneTranslatorIndex]` and compact charts. No such finite instance exists, and that index is not expected to be finite.
- [`compactSpace_glued_iff_quasiCompact`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0AtlasCompactFromClass.lean:320) applies definitionally but is only an equivalence, not a producer.

**Fresh HEAD commit**

[`PicRepDatum.toJacobianData`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean:83) is the newly landed theorem. `Jsc`, its `.2` representation, and the LFT theorem trivially form `PicRepDatum k k C`, but `toJacobianData` still takes `hqc`. [`toJacobianDataOfAbelLifts`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean:140) still takes residue-field-pinned Abel lifts. The commit is packaging, not a QC producer.

**FiniteInAffine**

- [`FiniteInAffine`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/FiniteInAffine.lean:32) only says every finite subset lies in an affine open.
- The affine, isomorphism, and affine-morphism criteria are at lines 36, 41, and 51; none applies to `Jsc`.
- [`finiteInAffine_of_isAlgClosed_of_irreducible`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/GroupAffineOpen.lean:162) can use the group object derived from `Jsc`’s representation and the known LFT theorem, but additionally requires `[IsAlgClosed k]` and `[IrreducibleSpace Jsc.left]`. Neither follows from the current `[IsSepClosed k]` endpoint.
- Even if obtained, `FiniteInAffine` does not imply quasi-compactness; its consumer is the Galois orbit condition at [`orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/FiniteInAffine.lean:66).

**Smallest honest missing lemma**

The strongest existing input is already landed:

- [`isLocallySurjective_abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0AdmissibleAbelEtaleSurjective.lean:72): the admissible Abel map from `D := divRepAffAdmissibleScheme C` is étale-locally surjective.
- [`quasiCompact_divRepAffAdmissibleScheme`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0AdmissibleDivisorQuasiProjective.lean:315): `D` is quasi-compact, hence `D.left` is compact.
- [`representableBySigmaIso`](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0SepClosedRepresentable.lean:63) turns `Jsc`’s representation into
  `yoneda.obj Jsc.left ≅ pic0SigmaSheaf C`.

Compose the admissible Abel map with that inverse to obtain an étale-locally-surjective map
`yoneda.obj D.left ⟶ yoneda.obj Jsc.left`. The missing generic bridge is:

```lean
theorem surjective_yonedaEquiv_of_isLocallySurjective_etale
    {X Y : Scheme} (φ : yoneda.obj X ⟶ yoneda.obj Y)
    [Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.etaleTopology φ] :
    Function.Surjective (yonedaEquiv φ).base
```

No project or mathlib declaration with this content exists. Mathlib’s `Scheme.geometricFiber` supplies the proof mechanism: apply its `jointly_surjective` field to the image sieve and a geometric point above each `y`. Once this bridge lands, `quasiCompact_of_surjective` immediately proves `QuasiCompact Jsc.hom`, and the already landed representation plus LFT theorem package the exact carrier into `JacobianData C`.
